title: The Last Garden Anew
premise: Silas Kavanagh survives by stealing memories—lifting them from travelers' minds and selling them to the memory-brokers of Thornfell—while keeping her own gift hidden from the world. When the crown's witch-hunters begin burning anyone touched by the old magic, Silas is forced to flee with a stolen memory that reveals the king died years ago and something ancient wears his face, sustained by the last living dragon-fire hidden beneath the royal gardens. Guided by a disgraced royal gardener and the king's estranged daughter, Silas must reach the garden before the fire gutters out and the creature becomes unkillable, discovering that her own stolen memories hold the key to unbinding the false king. In the end, Silas sacrifices her most precious memory—her mother's face—to feed the dragon-fire and burn the impostor away, choosing to build a new belonging rather than mourn the one she lost.
about_author: Ansel Delacroix is the pen name of a former botanist who abandoned a decade of greenhouse research to write fantasy about gardens, memory, and the things that grow in the dark. They live in a drafty farmhouse with too many cats and a stubborn wisteria that refuses, much like their protagonists, to stay where it's planted.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Silas Kavanagh lifts a smuggler's memories on a mountain pass, showing her gift's mechanics and the careful rules that keep her invisible. Her broker, Maren, warns that hunters have reached Thornfell. Silas dismisses it—until she finds a hunter's mark burned onto her own doorframe. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: uneasy comfort shattered by first true fear.

chapters.title: What the Broker Wouldn't Buy
chapters.summary: Desperate for coin, Silas steals a sealed memory-vial from a dying courier: a royal gardener's final recollection of the king's death and the thing that took his place. The vial's contents bleed into her mind, giving her knowledge she never asked for. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread as she realizes she now carries a death sentence.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Thornfell Road
chapters.summary: Witch-hunters sweep the mountain villages, and Silas watches her old fence dragged away in chains. Using smuggler roads she alone knows, she escapes Thornfell, but the stolen memory marks her—the hunters can sense it. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief for a community she never let herself belong to.

chapters.title: The Gardener of Ashes
chapters.summary: Silas tracks down Edric Hale, the disgraced royal gardener whose memory she carries, now living in exile. He recognizes his own recollections in her eyes and, after rage, agrees to help her reach the capital's hidden garden. POV: Edric. Emotional beat: bitter shame transformed into fragile purpose.

chapters.title: A Princess in a Wine Cellar
chapters.summary: In the border town of Vess, Silas and Edric find Princess Isolde hiding from her father's hunters—she suspects what her father has become. She joins them, bringing knowledge of the palace's forgotten ways. POV: Isolde. Emotional beat: guarded hope at finding allies who believe her.

chapters.title: Memories for Sale
chapters.summary: The trio trades Silas's stolen memories to a broker caravan for passage, and Silas watches strangers live pieces of other lives. Isolde confronts Silas about the ethics of her gift, sparking conflict. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: defensive pride cracking into uncomfortable self-examination.

chapters.title: The Thing That Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Through Edric's memory, the reader sees the full horror: the king dying in the garden while a creature of smoke and hunger drank his last breath and donned his shape. The false king announces a festival to celebrate the hunt's success. POV: Edric. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt finally given words.

chapters.title: River of Forgetting
chapters.summary: Crossing the Lethe River, hunters ambush the group. Silas uses her gift in the open for the first time, tearing the lead hunter's memories apart to save Isolde. The act binds them in trust but leaves Silas shaken by what she took. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of finally being seen.

chapters.title: The Garden Beneath
chapters.summary: Edric reveals the royal garden's secret: beneath it sleeps the last dragon, its fire the only thing that can unmake the creature. But the fire is guttering—the creature has been feeding on it for years. They must reach the dragon before the final ember dies. POV: Edric. Emotional beat: desperate hope against impossible odds.

chapters.title: What Silas Stole from Herself
chapters.summary: Isolde discovers Silas has stolen her own painful memories to survive—her mother's face, her childhood home. Silas confesses she no longer remembers why she's running, only that she must. POV: Isolde. Emotional beat: judgment softening into fierce compassion.

chapters.title: The False King's Mercy
chapters.summary: Captured and brought before the false king, Silas is offered freedom if she surrenders the stolen memory. The creature tempts her: it can return everything she's taken from herself. Isolde and Edric are thrown in the dungeons. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: temptation's seductive pull against nascent loyalty.

chapters.title: Chains in the Dark
chapters.summary: In the dungeon, Silas pretends to negotiate while stealing the jailer's memories to learn the garden's entrance. Edric, broken by returning to the palace, finds unexpected strength. POV: Edric. Emotional beat: quiet courage kindling in despair.

chapters.title: The Jailer's Forgotten Daughter
chapters.summary: Silas discovers the jailer's stolen memories include his daughter—whom Silas realizes was a memory she sold years ago, erasing the girl from his mind. She restores it, and the jailer opens the cells. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: guilt met with the first act of true restitution.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Burning Festival
chapters.summary: The false king's festival becomes a pyre as hunters burn the gifted publicly. The escaped trio moves through the chaos, Silas stealing memories from the fleeing crowds to mask their trail. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: horror and resolve intertwined.

chapters.title: Roots That Remember
chapters.summary: Edric leads them into the garden's hidden depths, where the plants themselves remember every hand that tended them. The garden recognizes its old gardener and opens the way down. POV: Edric. Emotional beat: reconciliation with a life's calling.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon
chapters.summary: They find the dragon, ancient and nearly extinguished, its fire barely a candle-flame. The dragon speaks in borrowed voices—memories it has absorbed for centuries—and tells Silas the creature can only be unbound by a memory freely given to the fire. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: awe and terrible understanding.

chapters.title: The Price of Unbinding
chapters.summary: The dragon explains the cost: the fire must be fed a memory of true love, freely surrendered. Silas realizes only her mother's face—her deepest stolen treasure, the thing that makes her herself—qualifies. Isolde begs her to find another way. POV: Isolde. Emotional beat: love demanding sacrifice it cannot bear to ask.

chapters.title: The Creature Ascendant
chapters.summary: The false king descends into the garden, the last ember flickering. He offers Silas her mother's face restored if she lets the creature consume the dragon and take its shape forever. Silas sees, at last, the truth: the thing cannot give what it only takes. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: clarity cutting through longing.

chapters.title: Feed the Fire
chapters.summary: Climax: Silas gives her mother's memory to the dragon-fire, which blazes back to life. The creature, wearing the king's screaming face, is unmade in the flame. Edric holds the garden gates, Isolde holds the line against hunters, and Silas holds nothing—empty and free. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: sacrifice transmuted into liberation.

chapters.title: Ashes and Acorns
chapters.summary: The dragon, restored, takes wing for the first time in centuries. Isolde claims the throne as regent, and Edric is reinstated as royal gardener. Silas, hollowed but unburdened, wanders the garden above, planting something new. POV: Edric. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude sharing the same soil.

chapters.title: A Memory Freely Given
chapters.summary: Isolde offers Silas a place at court; Silas instead chooses to rebuild the memory-broker trade as a guild of restitution, returning stolen memories across Thornfell. The dragon's fire, tended in the garden, becomes a hearth for the hunted. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: belonging chosen rather than stolen.

chapters.title: The Garden Anew
chapters.summary: A year later, Silas plants a tree over the dragon's old sleeping place, unable to remember her mother's face but able to imagine one. Isolde visits; Edric prunes; the fire burns steady. Silas finally understands inheritance is not what we keep, but what we grow. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace.
